title: The Toolchain can be generated from the ontology contract with security equivalence
claim: From the shared Ontology Language/IR, the system can generate typed object/query/function/action/agent surfaces for both domains so that new ordinary domain resources require no handwritten endpoint and expose exactly the capabilities allowed by the security model.
null_hypothesis: A useful developer/agent surface still requires bespoke endpoints and permission glue per domain; the ontology is not functioning as a backend/toolchain contract.
rivals: Generic GraphQL/REST schema generation provides the same result without ontology-specific machinery.
Generated surfaces exist but security/runtime semantics diverge from the core authorization oracle.
mechanism: Typed resource definitions contain enough shape/capability/security metadata to derive SDK types, query operations and governed Action tools mechanically.
scope: Manufacturing + Project Ontology object/link/interface/function/action resources and generated principal/capability combinations.
predictions: Adding a normal Project object/action requires zero handwritten API/tool endpoint code.
Generated SDK types preserve object/link/interface cardinalities and Function/Action distinction.
For every generated principal case, visible/queryable/actionable capabilities equal the independent authority oracle.
Agent tool surface excludes forbidden actions rather than relying on prompt obedience.
Interface-polymorphic tooling works for multiple implementing object types without type-specific endpoint additions.
falsifiers: A normal domain object/action needs a handwritten endpoint to become usable.
Generated surface exposes a capability denied by the authority oracle.
Generated surface hides an allowed capability because permission logic is duplicated incorrectly.
Interface polymorphism requires per-concrete-type tool code.

experiment.summary: Generate SDK/query/action/agent surfaces from frozen IR; compare type/security behavior against independent schema and authority oracles.
steps: Generate both domains from a clean toolchain build.
Diff handwritten code before/after adding selected ordinary Project resources.
Generate principals/permissions/object sets with Hypothesis and compare surface capabilities to authority oracle.
Run adversarial agent calls against hidden/denied capabilities.
Add two object types implementing one interface and test generic tooling.

oracle: Independent IR type checker plus independent authority/capability reference model.
baseline: Generic OpenAPI/GraphQL/typed-code generation over conventional schemas with equivalent authorization integration.

support_if: 0 handwritten endpoint/tool additions for preregistered ordinary Domain 2 resources.
100% type/cardinality/function-action conformance on generated surface tests.
100% capability-set equality with authority oracle across at least 10,000 generated principal cases.
0 forbidden external/canonical effects from adversarial agent calls.
Generic interface tool works across at least two implementing object types.
reject_if: Any preregistered ordinary resource requires bespoke endpoint/tool code or any security overexposure occurs.
inconclusive_if: Generated principal corpus below 10,000 or interface-polymorphism case not implemented.
invalid_if: Toolchain imports the authority oracle implementation directly, making differential security checks tautological.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate schemas, principals, resource sets, capabilities and agent requests; differential-test generated surface against independent type/security oracles.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Drop a property/cardinality, expose a denied action, suppress an allowed action and hard-code a concrete interface type; all must be detected.

stop_conditions: If ordinary resources repeatedly require handwritten endpoints, reject Toolchain-generation claim before building UI/convenience layers.
